exact_missing_items: Seam-level failure classes (10, formalized): GUI/runtime mismatch, incomplete end-to-end flow, cross-package state mismatch, contract drift, technically-wired-but-operationally-unusable, local-pass/global-fail composition, missing degraded/recovery behavior, inconsistent UX semantics, cross-seam architecture drift, invisible governance/missing operator affordances

Multi-account settings: user-configurable threshold for auto-switch; ON by default for all provider-using actors; granularity by provider, account, execution role; same-provider accounts with different quotas are NOT fungible

Lane is the primary operational object in Orchestrator; Worktree is the concrete filesystem/Git backing for a lane instance — lane identity persists after the live worktree is cleaned up/archived/removed
'suspect' and 'restoring' states are Orchestrator-first, Source Control-second — Orchestrator determines these states and Source Control reflects them
baseline: canonical starting lane for a package pool
active: currently eligible/in use for live work
suspect: not safe for normal dispatch until examined or restored
